free_text: The patient is a 71-year-old male with a rising PSA of 5.8 ng/mL and severe LUTS (IPSS 23/35). MRI shows a PI-RADS 4 lesion (cT1c) in the right transition zone. Histology confirms Gleason 3+4 (ISUP Grade Group 2). The management assessment is to review individual treatment benefit and preferences, balancing the risk of progression against potential treatment side effects.
